author: Jace O'Barto
title: 3 shootings in 3 days: Lexington leaders respond - NewsBreak
text:
By Jace O'Barto ,
2 hours ago LEXINGTON, Ky. ( FOX 56 ) — This week, there have been three consecutive shootings in Lexington in three consecutive days.
The first shoot was on Sunday, Sept. 28. One man was taken to the hospital with reported life-threatening injuries in an overnight shooting on the 100 block of Village Drive.
LATEST KENTUCKY NEWS: Then, on Monday, Sept. 29, around 7:30 p.m., Lexington police responded to a scene at the 600 block of Ohio Street, where a man was injured.
And on Tuesday night , around 8:15 p.m., officers were sent to the 500 block of E. Seventh Street for reports of a shooting with a victim. When they arrived, they found a male victim who was pronounced dead at the scene by the Fayette County Coroner.
The victim was identified in the coroner’s report as 19-year-old Ja’Zarion Robinson . His death is something Lexington Police said they’re continuing to investigate.
“Detectives and officers will be in the area for the next few days talking with residents and trying to find out more information about this incident,” said Sergeant Bige Towery, public information officer for the Lexington Police Department, in a video the department posted to Facebook.
According to data from the police department, Robinson’s shooting death marks the 17th homicide in Lexington this year. It was the only one in September; the first one since Aug. 11.
According to the data, there were five homicides last September. The cause of death for four of the victims was a gunshot, while the fifth homicide was due to blunt force.
Councilman Tyler Morton represents Lexington’s 1st District, which is where Robinson was killed.
I am deeply saddened by the senseless violence that claimed the life of a young man this week. My thoughts and prayers are with his loved ones as they face an unimaginable grief.
Every life lost to gun violence is a tragedy that sends shockwaves through families, neighborhoods, and our entire city. As a city and a community, we must do more to build safer and healthier neighborhoods, address the root causes of violence, invest in our youth, support the well-being of our residents, and ensure that everyone feels secure. I remain committed to advancing this work and strengthening the progress already underway.
May we carry the memories of those we have lost to gun violence as a guiding light, and honor their lives by working tirelessly toward a safer, more peaceful community.
Councilman Tyler Morton
Lexington Police are asking for the public’s help in finding the person responsible for Robinson’s death.
